Plot logbook coverage by flag and year

plot_logbook_coverage.Rd

Visualises logbook reporting coverage (as calculated by calculate_logbook_coverage()) as a flag x year heatmap, with each tile shaded by coverage and labelled with the coverage percentage. Facets by gear automatically if more than one gear is present in the data.

Usage

plot_logbook_coverage(coverage_data = NULL, ...)

Arguments

coverage_data

A tibble as returned by calculate_logbook_coverage(), containing at least FLAG_CODE, YY, and coverage columns (and optionally GEAR_CODE). If NULL (the default), calculate_logbook_coverage() is called using ....

...

Additional arguments passed to calculate_logbook_coverage() when coverage_data is NULL (e.g. in_wcpfc, flag, gear, species, year, group_species).

flag_order

Optional character vector giving the order flags should appear on the y-axis, top to bottom (as per ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = ...)). Defaults to descending mean coverage across the data.

Value

A ggplot object: a tile plot of year (x) by flag (y), filled by coverage (0-1, RdYlBu palette), with each tile labelled with its coverage as a percentage (or "X" where coverage is missing).

Details

Coverage is expected on a 0-1 scale, where 1 indicates full logbook coverage relative to ACE catch. Missing coverage (e.g. no ACE catch to compare against) is plotted as "X" rather than a percentage. Label colour switches between black and white depending on how far a tile's coverage sits from the midpoint of the colour scale, to keep text legible against both light and dark fills.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
calculate_logbook_coverage(in_wcpfc = TRUE, group_species = TRUE, gear = "L", year = 2004:2025) |>
  plot_logbook_coverage()

# or call calculate_logbook_coverage() implicitly
plot_logbook_coverage(in_wcpfc = TRUE, group_species = TRUE, gear = "S", year = 2004:2025)
} # }
